paragraph_changes.before: This Langyao-red Guanyin vase belongs to the Kangxi period and is held by the Palace Museum. Its striking copper-red glaze recalls earlier Ming porcelain, especially Xuande-period wares. Jingdezhen potters revived a technique that was difficult to fire successfully.
paragraph_changes.after: This Kangxi-period Langyao-red Guanyin vase is held by the Palace Museum. Langyao is a high-fired copper-red glaze named after Lang Tingji, the Jiangxi governor who supervised kiln production. Jingdezhen potters drew on Ming Xuande red glazes to develop a distinctive Qing glaze with a glassy surface and a pale rim.
